author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Students and staff at Rundlett Middle School in Concord are beginning a new academic year beside an active construction site, as work advances on the city’s replacement middle school. The project is close enough to the current building that classroom noise and vibration have become part of the daily routine.

Construction started before summer and moved into a busier phase as students returned for fall classes. The effects are most noticeable near the eighth-grade science wing and art rooms, where teachers have had to account for intermittent sound from heavy equipment and other work outside.

School administrators and teachers told the Concord Monitor that many students are adapting, while some have become curious about the machinery and progress next door. Staff are working to keep instruction steady and respond when construction activity becomes distracting.

The overlap is expected to continue through the roughly two-year building period. Keeping the existing school open allows classes to continue on site, but it also requires close coordination around safety, access and the learning environment. For families, the opening weeks offer the first sustained look at how the district will manage daily school operations while a major public project rises nearby.
dek: Construction beside Concord’s existing middle school is bringing noise and vibration, but staff say students are adjusting as the replacement building takes shape.
headline: Rundlett students adapt as new middle-school construction ramps up
